<!-- example-1: body_md -->
\label{ExmLimit}
  If $x^l+b_{l-1}x^{l-1}+\cdots+b_0$ is a Pisot polynomial, $b_l=1$, $k=a_0=0$, then \eqref{eq:SeqPoly} is a sequence of Salem polynomials.
<!-- end example-1 -->
<!-- theorem-1: body_md -->
\label{thmErdTur} (Erd\H{o}s, Tur\'{a}n) Let $F(x)=\sum_{k=0}^d a_kx^k\in \mathbb{C}[x]$ with $a_da_0 \ne 0$, and let
$$N(F;\alpha,\beta)=\#\{\textrm{roots}\;\;r\in \mathbb{C}\;\textrm{of}\;F\;\textrm{with}\;\alpha \le \arg(r)\le \beta\}.$$
Then for all $ 0\le \alpha<\beta \le 2\pi$,
$$\left|\frac{N(F;\alpha,\beta)}{d}-\frac{\beta-\alpha}{2\pi}\right|\le\frac{16}{\sqrt{d}}\left[\log\left(\frac{|a_0|+\cdots+|a_d|}{\sqrt{|a_0a_d|}}\right)\right]^{1/2}.$$
<!-- end theorem-1 -->
<!-- theorem-2: body_md -->
\label{ThmLimit}
If $k>0$ is an integer and $b_j=b_l-j$, $j=0,1,\ldots,l$ then for all fixed integers $a_j$, $j=1, \ldots,k$ there is a limit $C(P_{2n+2l})$ when $n$ tends to infinity.
<!-- end theorem-2 -->
<!-- e-definition-1: body_md -->
Let the limit of $C(P_{2n+2l})$ when $n$ tends to infinity be called limit ratio and denoted $LC(P_{2n+2l})$.
<!-- end e-definition-1 -->
<!-- example-2: body_md -->
\label{ExmLimit0}
Let $T_{2n+8,m}$ denote
$$T_{2n+8,m}(x)=x^{n+4}\left(\sum
_{j=0}^4 b_{j,m}\left(x^{n+j}+\frac{1}{x^{n+j}}\right) +2\right).$$
<!-- end example-2 -->
<!-- theorem-3: body_md -->
\label{ThmLimit0}
If we use the notation introduced in the previous example then $$\lim_{m\rightarrow \infty}LC(T_{2n+8,m}(x))=0.$$
<!-- end theorem-3 -->
<!-- lemma-1: body_md -->
\label{lemmaCOdd}
$$\sin \frac{t}{2}\left(\sum_{j=1}^{m} 2 \cos jt+1\right)=\sin \frac{(2m+1)t}{2}$$
<!-- end lemma-1 -->
<!-- lemma-2: body_md -->
\label{lemmaCEven}
$$\sin \frac{t}{2}\left(\sum_{j=1}^{m} 2 \cos \frac{(2j-1)t}{2}\right)=\sin mt$$
<!-- end lemma-2 -->
<!-- theorem-4: body_md -->
\label{ThmEnvelB1}
  If $b_0=b_1=\cdots=b_l=1$ is valid in \eqref{eq:SeqPoly} then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:Env}
  E(t)=\frac{\sin{\frac{(l+1)t}{2}}}{\sin \frac{t}{2}}.
\end{equation}
<!-- end theorem-4 -->
<!-- e-definition-2: body_md -->
Let $\varphi_A(x)$ denote the polynomial $(x^A-1)/(x-1)$, and write
$$P_{A,B}(x,y)=x^{\max(A-B,0)}(\varphi_A(x)+\varphi_B(x)y+x^{B-A}\varphi_A(x)y^2).$$
<!-- end e-definition-2 -->
<!-- example-3: body_md -->
Let $H_{2n+2l}(x)$ denote
$$H_{2n+2l}(x)=x^{n+l}\left(\sum
_{j=0}^l \left(x^{n+j}+\frac{1}{x^{n+j}}\right) +1\right).$$
<!-- end example-3 -->
<!-- theorem-5: body_md -->
\label{ThmFig1}
If $m$ is an integer greater than 1 then
  $$\frac{2}{\pi(2m+1)}\frac{\sin\frac{(m-1)\pi}{2m}}{\sin\frac{\pi}{2m}}<LC(H_{2n+2m-2}(x))<\frac{2}{6m-\pi}\frac{\sin\frac{(m-1)\pi}{2m}}{\sin\frac{\pi}{2m}}$$
<!-- end theorem-5 -->
<!-- corollary-1: body_md -->
If $A$ is an adherent point of the sequence $LC(P_{m,1}(x))_{m>1}$ then
  $$\frac{2}{\pi^2}\le A \le \frac{2}{3\pi}$$
<!-- end corollary-1 -->
<!-- conjecture-1: body_md -->
There is the limit of the sequence $LC(P_{m,1}(x))_{m>1}$ satisfying
\begin{equation}\label{eq:LimPm1}
\lim_{m\rightarrow \infty}LC(P_{m,1}(x))_{m>1}\approx 0.209.
\end{equation}
<!-- end conjecture-1 -->
<!-- conjecture-2: body_md -->
If $N$ is a natural number $\ge 1$ there is some $c(N)>0 $ such that any sequence $P_{2n+2l}$ of integer polynomials defined in \eqref{eq:SeqPoly}, having coefficients $\le N$ in modulus, that has the limit ratio strictly below $c(N)$ has the limit ratio equal to 0.
<!-- end conjecture-2 -->
